title: Electronic sign approved for Guelph Little Theatre
subtitle: Council also approved a semi-detached home at 25 Alice Street and a golf simulator rezoning on Hanlon Creek Boulevard.
overview: The most contested item was a sign variance for 176 Morris Street. Council approved an electronic message board 22.4 metres from a residentially zoned property, and approved signage in a park zone {{vote:m4}}. A nearby resident objected, citing light shining toward homes and a lack of demonstrated need. Staff said the sign's brightness is limited by the sign by-law, and that alternative locations could have a greater impact on neighbours.

Council also approved a zoning change at 25 Alice Street to allow a semi-detached dwelling {{vote:m1}}. It approved a rezoning at 585 Hanlon Creek Boulevard to allow a recreation facility, a golf simulator, in two units of a business plaza under construction {{vote:m5}}.

For residents, the sign decision sets a local example on how electronic signs near homes are judged. The other two approvals add housing and a new recreation use in existing planned areas. Council also passed a set of routine by-laws and adjourned at 7:16 p.m.

decisions.detail: Council approved an electronic message board 22.4 metres from a residentially zoned property, and signage in a park zone {{vote:m4}}.
Council approved rezoning to a specialized semi-detached/duplex residential zone to permit a semi-detached dwelling {{vote:m1}}.
Council received the application and approved specialized business park zones allowing a recreation facility, a golf simulator, in units 36 and 37 {{vote:m5}}.

debate: A delegate living across from the theatre opposed the sign. They said it would shine into nearby windows, that the 22-metre distance was very close, and that an electronic board does not suit the theatre's character.
The delegate also argued that no need had been shown, saying the street is a low-traffic residential one, and that a variance should have to be justified as minor and needed.

Staff said a ground sign was considered early on but would have a greater impact on residents. Other building locations could face the Morris Street homes more directly. Staff said permits limit brightness to a set level by day and a lower level after sunset.

One councillor tried to move refusal, citing concerns about precedent in a residential area and the lack of similar approved signs. The clerk advised that a refusal could not be an amendment to a motion to approve. Another councillor asked about the zone type, and staff confirmed it is a specialized park zone described as commercial recreation.

On the Hanlon Creek item, the planning consultant said the golf simulator is a complementary use taking a small share of total floor area. Staff reported that the four public comments received were supportive, and no councillors raised questions.
